body:
Gold's scanner turned up zero cross-platform arbitrage opportunities today, and that lines up with what's happening in the market: prices have been swinging hard day to day. Fortune's daily gold tracker put the metal at gold was trading at $4,331 per ounce at 9:10 a.m. Eastern Time on September 1, 2026, then Yahoo Finance reported Gold (GC=F) December futures opened at $4,436.40 per troy ounce on Thursday, September 3, 2026, up 0.5% compared to Wednesday's closing price, with the move attributed to hopes that a flare-up in the Iran conflict would stay contained. By Friday, September 4, futures had eased back to $4,521.40 per troy ounce as of 6:45 a.m. ET ahead of the jobs report. This kind of chop is consistent with the broader 2026 story of Fed rate-cut bets, dollar weakness, and heavy central-bank buying that analysts have been citing all year.

On the two platforms themselves, nothing screams free money. Kalshi's settle-style contracts (paying out on gold's official 5pm print) are quoted with reasonably tight spreads — the September 30 Above $4,370.99 contract sits at 0.58/0.62 with real volume behind it, and the year-end $4,400 or above strike is close by at 0.58/0.61. Polymarket's contracts are a different animal: most are "touch" markets that pay out if gold ever hits a level intraday, not just at settlement, and several of the weekly strikes (e.g., hit $4,400 Week of September 7) show bid/ask spreads as wide as 0.51 to 0.97. That gap is a thin-book problem, not an arbitrage signal — with almost no resting liquidity on one side, the quoted edge isn't actually fillable.

Bottom line: a quiet day for arbitrage, but not a quiet day for gold itself, which remains volatile in the low-$4,300s to mid-$4,500s amid geopolitical noise and rate-cut speculation.
headline: Gold arbitrage scanner finds nothing despite wild swings from $4,331 to $4,521
